channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Autora de gol do São Paulo, Bia Menezes celebra título: ‘Torcida merece’
item.description: Bia Menezes, scorer of São Paulo's goal, celebrated the 2026 Feminine Brasileirão title, highlighting the team's journey and fan support. The final against Corinthians set a record attendance for women's club football in Brazil and South America.

item.title: Lula tem 46,7% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 43,8%, na véspera da eleição, aponta pesquisa AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula (PT) leads with 46.7% and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) holds 43.8% in the AtlasIntel poll of October 3rd, keeping a lead beyond the ±1pp margin. In a simulated second round, they are statistically tied at 47.6% to 47.4%. The race reveals a sharply polarized electorate split by region, education, and religion.

item.title: Flávio lidera disputa presidencial no ES, diz pesquisa
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll released on October 3, 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading voter intentions in Espírito Santo with 48.8%, against Lula's 34.4% in the first round. In a hypothetical second-round matchup, Bolsonaro leads with 51.7% versus Lula's 39.2%.

item.title: Os números da pesquisa AtlasIntel sobre a disputa entre Lula e Flávio na véspera da eleição
item.description: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows Lula leading Flávio by 2.9 points ahead of the first round, with a simulated runoff indicating a technical tie between the two. Lula's government holds 46.8% approval among respondents.

item.title: Crise no STF, nó fiscal e Trump: profusão de desafios aguarda próximo governo
item.description: The next federal government will face a mix of historical and emerging challenges, including the STF crisis, the fiscal bottleneck, and international issues like Trump's influence. Experts emphasize the need to prioritize these topics on the national agenda to address structural problems affecting the Brazilian population for decades.

item.title: Lula tenta quarto mandato lutando contra desgaste de imagem após 44 anos em eleições
item.description: Lula, 80, is running for his seventh and likely final presidential election, facing image wear after 44 years of political highs and lows. His main challenge is overcoming voter fatigue and maintaining support in a polarized scenario.

item.title: Em estreia do Missão, Renan Santos fez campanha marcada por ataques e discurso radical
item.description: Renan Santos's campaign, representing the Missão party for president, was marked by direct attacks on Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, featuring an anti-system speech and radical positioning. The aggressive approach defines the candidate's debut in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Itamaraty corre perigo se Flávio Bolsonaro subir a rampa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposed that his brother Eduardo become chancellor and promised 'a cleaning' in Brazilian diplomacy, a statement considered toxic. The suggestion drew criticism for threatening the independence of Itamaraty and Brazil's foreign policy.

item.title: Muralistas traduzem tensão eleitoral em retratos para a Folha do domingo de eleição
item.description: Muralists Paulo Ito and Carlos Eduardo Doy (Sosek) created portraits of President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for Folha's Sunday edition released on the first round of the 2026 elections. The artworks reflect the electoral tension on the front pages and in the Politics section.

item.title: Lula tem 47,0% dos votos válidos ante 44,1% de Flávio, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll released on October 3, 2026, shows Lula with 47.0% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro's 44.1% in the first round, with a one-point margin of error. In a potential runoff, the race is tied, with Lula leading by 0.2 percentage points. Government approval for Lula is negative, with 52.5% disapproving of the president's performance.

item.title: O pêndulo da Câmara: Centrão fica sem lado para tentar ampliar o poder
item.description: The Centrão struggles to unite in 2026, with divisions among parties supporting Tarcísio de Freitas and Flávio Bolsonaro. Scandals involving leaders like Ciro Nogueira and federal police investigations weaken alliances, while the Bolsonaro base remains fragmented ahead of the presidential election.

item.title: PT faz live de 8 horas e pede 1º turno para já encerrar a 6 X 1
item.description: The PT held an 8-hour live stream, dubbed 'Lulaço', to mobilize supporters and call for Lula's immediate reelection in the first round of the 2026 elections. The broadcast featured ministers, economists, and presenters, emphasizing the importance of advancing in Congress with the approval of proposals, particularly ending the 6 x 1 schedule. Despite the strong campaign, Lula did not participate in the live stream, while his opponent Flávio Bolsonaro has also used live streams as a mobilization strategy.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula aposta em mobilização na rua, e Flávio se mostra otimista na reta final
item.description: On the eve of the first-round vote, the campaigns of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) seek a final boost for a potential runoff. Lula emphasizes street mobilization, while Flávio projects optimism about his electoral path.

item.title: Quem são todos os candidatos a deputado federal por Sergipe (SE) nas eleições 2026
item.description: Over 1.74 million eligible voters in Sergipe will choose among 141 candidates for federal deputy in the 2026 elections, with 20 deemed ineligible. The state will elect 8 representatives to the Chamber of Deputies in a single-round vote on October 4, using a proportional system.

item.title: Datafolha no DF: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 49% das intenções de voto e Lula 37%
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on October 3, 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading voter intentions in the Federal District with 49%, followed by Lula (PT) at 37%. In the second round, Flávio maintains the lead with 55% against Lula's 38%.

item.title: Flávio usa última live antes da votação para defender impeachment de ministros do STF e dar espaço a Douglas Ruas
item.description: In his final livestream before the first round, Flávio Bolsonaro urged voters to elect senators supporting Supreme Court minister impeachments and highlighted allied candidates, including Douglas Ruas, who criticized Eduardo Paes. He emphasized the need for an independent legislature to oversee the judiciary and pushed for split-ticket voting to shape the Senate.

item.title: AtlasIntel: Lula marca 50,1% contra 49,9% de Flávio Bolsonaro em 2º turno
item.description: AtlasIntel poll shows Lula at 50.1% vs. Flávio Bolsonaro at 49.9% in a hypothetical runoff, tied within the margin of error. Total votes include 5% blank, null, and undecided.

item.title: AtlasIntel: Lula tem 47% e Flávio, 44,1%, dos votos válidos em 1º turno
item.description: AtlasIntel poll released on October 3 shows Lula with 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 44.1% of valid votes in the first round. The survey, with a 1 percentage point margin of error, interviewed 4,945 voters between September 27 and October 2.

item.title: Capitalismo destruiu o jantar em família, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from the Missão party, claimed in a podcast that capitalism weakens traditional habits like family dinners, linking it to industrialization and women's liberation. He used concepts from Deleuze, Guattari, and Mark Fisher to argue that the economic system reconfigures social meanings.

item.title: O que dizem as últimas pesquisas para presidente
item.description: The latest polling data for the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election shows a tightly contested race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with slight variations across different polling firms. The Quaest survey shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45% of valid votes, while Datafolha reports Lula at 45% and Bolsonaro at 42%. According to the CNT/MDA poll, Lula leads outside the margin of error. The overall picture points to an open and unpredictable race, with minimal differentiation between the two main contenders.

item.title: Lula e Flávio chegam à eleição em campanha ofuscada por escândalos, crise no STF e até guerra santa
item.description: The 2026 election campaign is marked by corruption scandals and STF crisis, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro as the only viable candidates. Polls show a technical tie between the two, both facing high disapproval rates. The race is described as 'the rejeição dispute,' reflecting low voter enthusiasm.

item.title: Pesquisa Atlas: Lula tem 47% dos votos válidos contra 44,1% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno
item.description: The Atlas/Bloomberg poll released before the first round shows Lula leading with 47% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro's 44.1%, a 2.9-point gap. In a simulated runoff, the two candidates are statistically tied.

item.title: Lula enfrentará seu principal adversário: ele mesmo
item.description: President Lula faces significant internal challenge with 54% of voters opposing his re-election. Tied with Flávio Bolsonaro, he must convince voters about his administration marked by scandals and criticism. The election becomes a referendum on his continuation in office.

item.title: Ministro do TSE cassa candidatura de Deltan ao Senado na véspera da eleição
item.description: The TSE minister canceled Deltan Dallagnol's Senate candidacy registration in Paraná on the eve of the election. The decision was announced by the Superior Electoral Court, directly affecting the electoral race in the state.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos que mais usaram dinheiro próprio na campanha
item.description: Gelson Merísio (PSB), candidate for governor of Santa Catarina, leads the list of candidates who most used personal funds in the 2026 elections, with R$1.15 million. Among the top ten self-funders, six are running for state offices, including figures such as Wilson Grassi (Democrats) and Kiko Caputo (Novo). Political parties and national directories are the main sources of additional funding.

item.title: Dallagnol diz que PT quer usar Gilmar para interferir na eleição
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol accuses the PT of trying to use Supreme Court minister Gilmar Mendes to interfere in the election, following a motion to nullify votes in his favor. He criticizes parallel legal strategies, viewing them as an attack on democracy.

item.title: Goleira do São Paulo declara ao vivo na Globo: “Bolsonaro nunca mais”
item.description: São Paulo goalkeeper Carlinha declared live on TV Globra after winning the 2026 Women's Brasileirão title: 'Bolsonaro never again in power'. Her statement occurred during the final broadcast between São Paulo and Corinthians, where she was one of the main figures of the match.

item.title: Quaest no AP, votos válidos: Dr Furlan, 53%; Clécio, 47%
item.description: A Quaest poll released on October 3rd, the day before the first round of the Amapá state elections, shows Dr Furlan (PSD) leading with 53% of valid votes against Clécio Luís (União Brasil) at 47%. The survey has a margin of error of 2 percentage points and a 95% confidence level, interviewing 1,800 voters. Among respondents, 89% say they have made a definitive voting decision.

item.title: A distância entre Lula e Flávio nas principais pesquisas eleitorais na véspera da eleição
item.description: Datafolha and Quaest surveys show a technical tie between Lula and Flávio in the first round, with Lula slightly ahead. The escalation of the election campaign and judicial decisions influenced the race, including the cancellation of the debate on TV Globo.

item.title: Segundo turno das eleições 2026: Flávio tem 44% das intenções de voto, enquanto Lula marca 42%, diz Quaest
item.description: The latest Quaest poll before the first round of the 2026 elections shows a technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), with 44% and 42% of voting intentions, respectively, in the second round. Both first-round simulations remain tied within the two-point margin of error.

item.title: A acirrada disputa na Bahia em última pesquisa antes do 1º turno
item.description: A new Quaest poll released on the eve of the first round shows a technical tie between incumbent governor Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) at 52% and former mayor ACM Neto (União Brasil) at 48% for the Bahia governorship. The 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level place both candidates on the same footing. The survey polled 2,004 voters between October 2-3, 2026, excluding blank, null, and undecided votes.

item.title: Quaest: Zucco tem 52% na disputa pelo governo do RS contra 35% de Juliana Brizola; aliado de Leite marca 12%
item.description: A new Quaest poll shows federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL) leading the race for governor of Rio Grande do Sul with 52% of valid votes, followed by Juliana Brizola (PDT) at 35% and Gabriel Souza (MDB) at 12%, an ally of Eduardo Leite. The strong performance of Zucco and Brizola complicates Leite's succession, whose administration is split, with 42% approval and 45% disapproval among voters. The survey uses the 'likely voter' model to estimate electoral behavior based on motivation and turnout history.

item.title: Datafolha para presidente em PE, votos válidos: Lula, 65%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 26%; Cury, 3%; Renan, 2%; Caiado, 2%
item.description: The Datafolha poll for president in Pernambuco, released on October 3, shows Lula with 65% of valid votes and Flávio Bolsonaro with 26%. Augusto Cury, Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema round out the top five, all with under 3%.

item.title: Quaest: na véspera da eleição, de Toni marca 17%, Carlos Bolsonaro 16%, e Amin 15% no Senado em SC
item.description: On the eve of the Senate election in Santa Catarina, a Quaest poll shows a technical tie among the three leading candidates: Carol de Toni (PL) with 17%, Carlos Bolsonaro (PL) with 16%, and Esperidião Amin (PP) with 15%. The race has been marked by intense attacks between Carlos Bolsonaro and Amin, especially after Jorginho Mello's indication of a 'pure blood' ticket composed of Bolsonaro and Carol de Toni, leaving the PP senator out. The poll, registered with the TSE, considers voter engagement to calculate valid votes.

item.title: Ministro do TSE derruba candidatura de Deltan Dallagnol ao Senado
item.description: TSE minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques overturned Deltan Dallagnol's Senate candidacy in Paraná, nullifying votes cast for him. The ruling, issued after an appeal by the 'Paraná for All' coalition, reverses the prior approval by the state electoral court and finds no new evidence to override Dallagnol's ineligibility under the Clean Record Act. Votes for Dallagnol will be counted as null in Sunday's election results.

item.title: Quaest para o Senado no AP, votos válidos: Rayssa Furlan, 30%; Randolfe Rodrigues, 21%; Lucas Barreto 21%
item.description: The Quaest poll released before the first round of Senate elections in Amapá shows Rayssa Furlan (Podemos) leading with 30% of valid votes, followed by Randolfe Rodrigues (PT) and Lucas Barreto (PSD), both at 21%. Acácio Favacho (MDB) comes in at 20%, followed by Alliny Serrão (União Brasil) with 8%.

item.title: Quaest: 49% desaprovam governo Lula, enquanto 44% aprovam
item.description: The Quaest survey shows that 49% of voters disapprove of President Lula's government, while 44% approve it, reflecting a slight downward trend within the margin of error. Despite recent measures such as increasing Bolsa Família benefits, banning online betting platforms, and expanding access to diabetes and obesity medications through SUS, the government's approval ratings have remained relatively stable. For 42% of respondents, the administration is rated negatively, compared to 33% who rate its performance positively.

item.title: Veja os números dos candidatos ao Senado no Rio Grande do Sul
item.description: Thirteen candidates compete for two Senate seats in Rio Grande do Sul in 2026. Ric Jones (PCO) has an undeferred registration within the appeal deadline and remains under judicial review, allowed to stay on the ballot per TSE guidance. The race proceeds with eligible candidates moving forward.

item.title: Veja como foi o último dia de campanha dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: On the final campaign day, candidates held walks, rallies, and closing events, emphasizing proposals on economy, health, and education. Lula stressed democracy defense, while Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the STF and projected confidence in victory. Samara, Augusto Cury, Hertz Dias, and others conducted regional activities to mobilize supporters.

item.title: Por decisão judicial, Folha tira do ar Datafolha para o Governo do CE
item.description: Folha de S.Paulo removed Datafolha survey from the air regarding the Ceará State Government after a judicial decision by electoral appeals judge Francisco Luís Rios Alves. The suspension occurred due to a formal issue in the registration, not flaws within the survey itself. The case was registered under numbers CE-09234/2026 and BR-06469/2026 at TSE.

item.title: Quaest: na véspera do 1º turno, Lula oscila para baixo e perde 'gás' entre católicos após polêmica sobre Nossa Senhora
item.description: A Quaest survey released Saturday, the eve of the first round, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) dropped four points and lost support among Catholics following a controversy involving Our Lady of Aparecida. Among evangelicals, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) rose from 46% to 50%, while Lula moved slightly upward to 28%.

item.title: No 2º turno, Lula tem 47% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 46%, indica Datafolha
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll before the first round of the 2026 presidential elections shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the second round, with 47% and 46% respectively. The one-point difference falls within the margin of error, keeping voters split between the two candidates.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro inicia último ato de rua antes do 1º turno ao lado de aliados no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) began his final street rally before the first round in the western zone of Rio de Janeiro. The campaign mobilizes allies and maintains a strong conservative appeal.

item.title: Horário dos locais de votação: portões abrem às 8h e fecham às 17h
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) established that polling stations will open at 8 AM and close at 5 PM on election Sunday, with a unified schedule following Brasília time. Voters must bring ID with photo and can check their voting location in advance.

item.title: Alcolumbre busca no TSE caminho para vitória de seu candidato no Amapá
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcômbreira is maneuvering at the TSE to secure victory for his gubernatorial candidate in Amapá, Clécio Luís, opposing the polls leader Dr. Furlan. The dispute involves Supreme Court justices Dias Toffoli and André Mendonça, with injunctions affecting Furlan's candidacy. The election is critical for Alcômbreira, who has previously lost other races in the state.

item.title: Com 68% dos votos válidos, Fonteles caminha para reeleição no 1º turno no Piauí, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: The AtlasIntel survey shows that Governor Rafael Fonteles (PT) leads with 65.1% of voting intentions for Piauí state government, against 28.2% for Joel Rodrigues (PP). With 68.4% of valid votes, Fonteles would secure a first-round victory, while his administration approval stands at 68%.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro monitora diplomatas e amplia pressão sobre Itamaraty
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) has intensified criticism of Itamaraty diplomats on social media, naming officials such as Vanessa Dolce de Faria and Orlando Leite Ribeiro, investigating alleged ties to the Lula administration and accusations of sabotaging the Bolsonaro government. Simultaneously, he reinforces promises of reforms in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under a potential Flávio Bolsonaro government.

item.title: Ato de Lula em SP reúne milhares e tem promessa do fim da 6 X 1
item.description: Lula closed his campaign for the first round with a walk in São Paulo, reaffirming the promise to approve the end of the 6 X 1 workday in the Senate. First Lady Janja spoke, emphasizing women's role in the victory and supporting the running mate Lula. The pension issue was central, with mentions of cases like Benedito de Almeida and former President Bolsonaro.

item.title: Equipe de segurança de Lula barrou contagem da USP para ato em São Paulo
item.description: Lula's security team blocked the USP Political Debate Monitor from counting attendees at an event near Avenida Paulista, citing security concerns and restricted airspace. The event took place on Rua Augusta after electric trucks were banned from Paulista Avenue and featured Geraldo Alckmin, Fernando Haddad, Márcio França, Simone Tebet, and Marina Silva. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro held a motorcycle parade in the interior of São Paulo.

item.title: Pesquisa Palver mostra liderança de Flávio Bolsonaro contra Lula
item.description: A Palver poll of 5,000 interviews shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 47% in the first round, followed by Lula (PT) at 43%. In the second round, the race remains tight with slight variations.
